questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant clusters need strict API access control; SPIFFE identity ensures only trusted services can perform sensitive calls. Gatekeeper + OPA enforces runtime policy with centralized visibility.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- SPIFFE IDs and SVIDs
- Kubernetes API verbs and RBAC implications
- Validation via audit logs and Gatekeeper status

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapicnst
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
      rego: |
        package k8sapi
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
          not allowed_spiffe(input.review.object)
          msg := sprintf("Pod %s in namespace %s cannot use API verb %s", [input.review.object.metadata.name, input.review.object.metadata.namespace, input.review.operation])
        }
        allowed_spiffe(pod) {
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"] in data.constraint.spec.allowedSVIDs
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sApiConstraint
metadata:
  name: restrict-api-verbs
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  allowedSVIDs:
    - "spiffe://ibm.com/workload/web"
    - "spiffe://tesla.com/workload/monitor"
    - "spiffe://cloudflare.com/workload/edge"
```

## Validation Plan
1. Deploy ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
2. Test compliant GET request from approved SPIFFE ID
3. Test noncompliant POST request from unapproved SPIFFE ID
4. Verify denial in Gatekeeper audit logs
5. Confirm monitoring namespace bypass works correctly

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical hardening policies across CI and runtime, not just definitions.

## Key Concepts
- Kyverno policy drafting, matches, and deny rules
- Pod security basics: readOnlyRootFilesystem, allowPrivilegeEscalation, capabilities
- CI/CD integration and runtime admission flow; namespace-based exceptions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-container-hardening
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: deny-privileged-containers
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    deny:
    - conditions:
      - key: '{{request.object.spec.containers[*].securityContext.privileged}}'
        operator: Equals
        value: 'true'
  - name: enforce-secure-rootfs
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    deny:
    - conditions:
      - key: '{{request.object.spec.containers[*].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem}}'
        operator: NotIn
        value: ['true']
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests basic security gating in a beginner-friendly way that ties manifest hardening to CI.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes securityContext fields
- kube-score risk levels (low/medium/high/critical)
- CI gate integration and failure semantics

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: alpine:3.18
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: false
      privileged: true
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: alpine:3.18
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      runAsUser: 1000
      privileged: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
name: kube-score gate
on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  kube-score:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install kube-score
        run: |
          curl -L -o kube-score https://github.com/zegl/kube-score/releases/download/v1.9.0/kube-score-1.9.0-linux-amd64
          chmod +x kube-score
          sudo mv kube-score /usr/local/bin/kube-score
      - name: Run kube-score
        run: kube-score score manifests/ --output json > kube-score.json
      - name: Fail on high risk
        run: |
          if grep -q high kube-score.json || grep -q critical kube-score.json; then
            echo High-risk issues found
            exit 1
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you scale this to multiple repos?
- How would you handle false positives?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to translate security requirements into policy-as-code, enforce across workload types, and validate in CI. It also probes tool choice (Kyverno vs OPA Gatekeeper), namespace scoping, and test design.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime security posture with securityContext fields
- Policy engines: Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper
- Resource types: Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets
- Local and CI validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno cluster policy example
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-runtime-hardening
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-secure-pod
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ['Deployment','StatefulSet','DaemonSet']
    validate:
      message: 'Containers must be non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - name: '*'
                securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  runAsUser: 1000
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ['ALL']
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest example (violates rules)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: fail-noncompliant
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: fail
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 0
          privileged: true
          capabilities:
            add: ['NET_ADMIN']
      volumes:
      - name: data
        hostPath:
          path: /data
```

```yaml

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: compliant
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:

        image: example/app:1.2.3

          runAsNonRoot: true
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question rigorously tests practical CI security knowledge for multi-tenant infrastructure, covering both container images and WASM modules deployed across edge and cloud environments. It evaluates understanding of supply chain security, provenance verification, and admission control policies.

## Key Concepts
- **Cosign Verification**: Cryptographic signing and verification for OCI container images and WASM modules using key pairs
- **SBOM Enforcement**: Requiring Software Bill of Materials for dependency transparency and vulnerability tracking
- **Rekor Attestations**: Immutable transparency log verification for artifact provenance
- **Manifest Validation**: Ensuring Kubernetes manifests reference only cryptographically verified signed artifacts
- **Admission Control**: Kyverno or OPA policies for runtime enforcement in Kubernetes clusters
- **GitHub Actions**: CI/CD workflow implementation for automated security gates

## Implementation Overview
The solution requires:
1. Cosign key pair management with public key distributed across CI/CD and cluster admission controllers
2. SBOM generation during build (using tools like Syft or SPDX)
3. Rekor integration for attestation verification
4. Policy engine (Kyverno/OPA) to validate signed references at admission time
5. Local developer verification scripts using cosign CLI

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime, policy-driven security for multi-tenant clusters, including per-tenant exceptions, scalable policy storage, and practical CI validation.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Rego enforcement
- Runtime security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, hostPath, privileged, SETUID checks
- Central PolicyStore for per-tenant overrides
- CI validation: dry-run, Gatekeeper evaluation, and manifest validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: runtimepolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RuntimePolicy
        listKind: RuntimePolicyList
        plural: runtimepolicies
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package runtimepolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
        msg := "container must run as non-root"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        any_cont := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not any_cont.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "container must have readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      }
      # Additional rules for hostPath, privileged, and SETUID would follow similarly
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Matters
This tests your ability to design supply chain security for a Kubernetes monorepo where multiple services share base images - a critical skill for CKS certification and real-world cluster security.

## Core Concepts

**Signing vs Attesting:**
- **Signing** (cosign sign): Cryptographically proves an image hasn't been tampered with since it was built and signed
- **Attesting** (cosign attest): Attaches signed metadata (SBOM, provenance) to an image that can be verified later

**SBOM (Software Bill of Materials):**
- Lists all components, packages, and dependencies in an image
- Generated with: `syft image -o spdx-json`
- Standard formats: SPDX, CycloneDX
- Critical for vulnerability scanning and compliance

**SLSA Provenance:**
- Tracks the entire build pipeline (SLSA Level 3+)
- Contains "materials" field that references base image digest
- Enables tracing derived images back to their bases
- Predicate type: `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`

**OCI Referrers:**
- Modern way to store attestations alongside images in OCI-compliant registries
- Replaces older annotation-based approaches
- Supported by Harbor, GHCR, ECR, ACR, GCR

**Policy Enforcement:**
- **Kyverno:** Native Kubernetes policy engine with verifyImages rule
- **OPA/Conftest:** General-purpose policy as code
- Run in CI/CD (before `helm upgrade`) AND optionally as admission controllers

**Key Security Properties:**
1. **Base image integrity:** Verify base images are signed and attested
2. **Derivation chain:** Service images must reference an attested base
3. **Immutable records:** Rekor transparency log ensures no retroactive changes
4. **Automated enforcement:** No deployment without verified images

Tests basic security posture enforcement in manifests, a real-world gate that beginners can implement with standard policy engines.

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (minimal)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secctx
spec:
  rules:
  - name: check-security
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet", "DaemonSet", "Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must set runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:

                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: foo
spec:

      - name: app
```

## Why This Is Asked
Real-world multi-tenant data platforms require strong admission control to enforce image provenance and host security postures across clouds. Gatekeeper with Rego enables centralized policy with testable manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Open Policy Agent Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint objects
- Image provenance: registry, non-latest, digest
- Pod hardening: resources, securityContext, privilegeEscalation
- Namespace labeling and admission scope
- CI validation: conftest, gatekeeper audit, sample manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (ImageProvenanceAndSecurity)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: imageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: ImageProvenanceConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package imageprovenance
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          some i
          container := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i]
          image := container.image
          startswith(image, "registry.example.com/")
          not endswith(image, ":latest")
          some digest := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i].imageDigest
          msg := "image must be from registry.example.com with digest"
        }
```
```yaml
# Constraint (ImageProvenanceConstraint)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ImageProvenanceConstraint
metadata:
  name: require-provenance
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
```

```yaml

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor

spec:
```

```yaml

kind: Deployment
```
